Seq2seq resolved to exactly its two consumed components: the cell (LSTM 1997 - both encoder and decoder are built from it) and the decoder formulation (Mikolov's RNNLM 2010 - the paper defines its decoder as an RNNLM conditioned on the input). The sharpest coeval artifact so far: Cho et al.'s RNN Encoder-Decoder (arXiv June 2014 vs seq2seq September 2014), the single most direct predecessor, dropped at the year bound together with 8 other 2014 artifacts (Devlin NNJM, GRU, Neural Turing Machines, Memory Networks, the WMT'14 dataset itself, dropout, conditional VAE, Chandar et al.) - at year granularity the template seq2seq scaled is unrepresentable as its predecessor. Recipe components behaved as designed: gradient clipping and teacher forcing passed directness (both literally in the paper's training procedure) but failed the Q1/Q2 gate on honest partials - components of a leap, not leaps. Generic substrate rejected as such: backpropagation, BPTT, SGD, CUDA. Two existing nodes (Bidirectional RNNs, Graves soft window) were scouted and matched but rejected for this parent - Sutskever's encoder is a unidirectional LSTM over reversed input, so no false convergence edges; both remain correctly attached at Bahdanau. NPLM rejected as mediated via the RNNLM, its consumed descendant.

BRNN resolved to its single consumed component: the Elman network (1990), the 'regular recurrent neural network' the paper explicitly extends in two directions. One-survivor expansion, like GPT-2's. Coeval artifact: LSTM (1997) dropped at the year bound - BRNN and LSTM are same-year siblings and their famous combination (BLSTM) waited until 2005, so at year granularity the cell BRNN would later marry is unrepresentable at this level. The forward-backward algorithm was graded directness=partial - the two-pass template is structurally identical to HMM smoothing and the authors worked in that tradition, but the paper presents the construction architecturally without citing it; partial fails the gate honestly rather than forcing a verdict. The Elman advance arrived twice in scouting (as 'Elman recurrent network' and as 'Finding structure in time', its own paper title); the second was filed as mediated via the first so the graph keeps exactly one Elman node. TDNN rejected as the overcome prior state (the paper defines itself against the preset future frame); substrate discipline maintained (BPTT/backprop/SGD/Fourier rejected as generic machinery).

survivors_detail.name: Pascal-Fermat correspondence on the problem of points (1654)
survivors_detail.status: NEW (depth 13 - the run's first depth-13 node)
survivors_detail.note: The session-56/58 assigned direct hearing, discharged as an admission. The channel is documented in the primary record: Huygens heard of the correspondence's problems in Paris in 1655 (from Carcavi's circle; he met Roberval and Mylon, not Pascal), was not told the methods or solutions, reconstructed them himself, and verified his Proposition XIV against Fermat through Mylon and Carcavi in 1656 (letter to Carcavi, 12 October 1656). The tract's problem-set IS the correspondence's: Props. III-IX are the points problem; the five closing problems are in part Fermat's and Pascal's; the last (Gambler's Ruin) stems from the correspondence resumed in 1656. Judged as an artifact (the letters), not a person-channel: what arrived was the founding content (the problems and the two solution routes' existence), per the Ferraro discrimination. Q1/Q2/Q3/Q5/Q6/Q10/Q11/Q12 pass; Q4/Q7/Q8 partial (no cost collapse in the letters themselves; no interface; reach beyond games performed by the tract); Q9 fail. Verification: four attacks run (channel attack - Huygens never read the letters, rebutted on the problem-set identity + the dated 1656 junction; multiples attack on Q3, scoped to descent of the problem-set; leap-inflation attack on the sample-space gloss, rebutted on Fermat's own device; reversed component attack on the two routes) - outcome provisional per standing practice.

Pascal's recursive expectation method (1654) - MEDIATED via the correspondence, same ground: the recursion is one of the two routes the letters contain; Huygens founds expectation on his own fair-exchange postulate, not on Pascal's text, which he never saw.

De Meree's gaming problems (1654) - MEDIATED via the correspondence: the channel runs questions -> Pascal -> correspondence -> tract; de Mere proposed no method, and the problems were the tradition's standing problems (in print since Pacioli 1494). Instance + motive at one remove (the Sears-at-Howard shape), the posing recorded in full.

CARDANO, Liber de Ludo Aleae - DATE-DROPPED at resolve (both filings, L1/L7), and the substantive record stands in the dropped list and here: filed at its graph-conventional year 1663 (the dating session 58 itself established - written in fragments c. 1525-1565, discovered among his papers posthumously, first printed in the 1663 Opera Omnia), the year bound drops it against the 1657 parent before any merits hearing, exactly as the print chronology foreclosed it at Bernoulli. The circulation record fetched this session makes the merits moot on the documents in any case: no source documents any circulation of the manuscript to Huygens, Pascal or Fermat (the one thin claim that Galileo 'seems to have read a copy' concerns an unpublished reader of an unpublished text). Anticipation/parallel, NOT a channel - the brief's anticipated outcome, reached by the calendar rather than by evaluation.
